ticket_title: [Blazor][MSI] DateTime columns display time by default - DataGridView
strengths: Excellent supporting evidence: Two complete example projects (WinForms original + migrated Blazor) with embedded screenshots showing visual comparison
Clear user story format with well-defined problem statement comparing Blazor vs WinForms behavior
Reasonable acceptance criteria that are mostly testable (4 distinct criteria covering functionality and testing)
Strong business prioritization with high value (4/4) and priority (2) indicating importance
Related work items tracked and linked, showing awareness of ecosystem
Already resolved with PR #119948 and commit linked, demonstrating progress
Technical comparison provides clear context for developers migrating from WinForms
weaknesses: No story points or time estimation assigned - critical planning gap for sprint commitment
Business context is implicit rather than explicit - no statement of user impact or business value justification
Incomplete risk assessment - no discussion of breaking changes to existing Blazor applications
Acceptance criteria uses vague language: 'specified format' is ambiguous - which format? Customizable per-column?
Relationship between 4 related linked items (791407, 791408, 790224, 791403) not documented - are they blockers or dependencies?
Cultural/localization considerations not addressed - how should different locales be handled?
Missing technical scope clarification: applies to all DateTime columns or only specific types?
No migration strategy or rollback plan documented for deployed systems
red_flags: CRITICAL: Zero story points assigned despite being Committed status - indicates estimation was skipped
CRITICAL: 'specified format' language in AC3 is vague and could cause implementation rework
Unspecified format behavior could lead to scope creep - developers may debate which format to use
Silent assumptions about WinForms behavior expected to be known - not all developers may have WinForms experience
Four related items without explanation suggests possible hidden dependencies or coordination needs
No explicit rollback/contingency plan if change breaks production Blazor applications
suggested_questions: What is the 'specified format' referenced in AC2? Should it match WinForms 'short' format, be customizable per-column, or respect user locale?
Will this change affect existing deployed Blazor applications? What is the migration path for applications currently relying on long format?
Should DateTime formatting be configurable per-column or column-group, or is a single application-wide format acceptable?
What is the relationship between the 4 related items (791407, 791408, 790224, 791403)? Are any blocking? Must they be completed first?
Does this apply only to date-only DateTime columns, or also to DateTime fields that include time components? How should time-only fields be handled?
What are the specific unit and integration test coverage requirements? How many test cases are needed for acceptable quality?
Is the 'MSI' tag a product line? Does this scope apply to all Blazor DataGridView implementations or only within MSI?
Should the format be configurable at application startup, per-grid, or per-column to maintain flexibility?
recommendations: URGENT: Add story point estimation before next sprint - this ticket is Committed but has zero points
Clarify format specification in AC: specify exact format string (e.g., 'MM/dd/yyyy') or behavior (WinForms equivalent, culture-aware, etc.)
Document risk mitigation: add section addressing backward compatibility and breaking changes for existing deployed applications
Explain dependencies: clearly document the relationship of the 4 related items - blocker, sequential, or parallel work?
Add technical scope boundaries: clarify whether this affects all DateTime columns, specific data types, or is configurable per-column
Include localization strategy: how should different cultures/locales handle date formatting (invariant, CultureInfo-aware, customizable)?
Add rollback criteria: define decision point and steps for reverting if production issues occur after deployment
Consider splitting out a separate task for format configuration design if it requires decisions beyond simple WinForms parity
